Philip K. Dick Reviews Herman Wouk's The Caine Mutiny is the canonical works-table record for PKD's primary text corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is Philip K. Dick Reviews Herman Wouk's The Caine Mutiny (Time, October 3, 1955) (1955-10-03).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: A scanned single-page document identified as Philip K. Dick's review of Herman Wouk's novel The Caine Mutiny, published in Time magazine on October 3, 1955. No OCR text layer is present.

This represents a rare early example of Dick's work as a critic and reviewer rather than a fiction writer. A book review in Time magazine indicates a level of mainstream literary engagement that is unusual in Dick's biography, as he is primarily known as a science fiction writer who operated outside the literary establishment. The Caine Mutiny, Wouk's 1951 Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about a naval mutiny, deals with themes of authority, paranoia, and institutional power that resonate with Dick's own fictional preoccupations. This document provides valuable evidence of Dick's engagement with mainstream literature in the mid-1950s.
